text:
maria: Quick heads-up — the Go SDK generator/streaming helpers are awkward when you need ctx propagation + auth-retry. Running into a pattern where I set a timeout on ctx but the stream goroutine keeps running after cancel. :confused:

joel: can you paste the minimal repro? usually it's a bug around using context.Background() in spawned goroutines.

maria: here you go:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator.Start(ctx, opts) // returns io-like stream
go func() {
  for {
    msg, _ := stream.Recv() // internal loop uses its own ctx sometimes
    // do work
  }
}()
```

joel: yep looks like Start spawns a loop that calls transport.Stream(ctx2) where ctx2 is tied to auth-refresh flow, not the caller ctx. so cancel doesn't reach the recv loop.

sara: we hit this on the onboarding sample app too — users rely on context cancellation to stop background work when they close requests. suggestion: provide a StreamWithParent(ctx, ...) helper that ensures the internal recv loop uses the caller ctx (and surface Close/Wait semantics).

matt: API suggestion:
```go
// returns handle that enforces propagation and exposes lifecycle controls
handle := client.Generator.StreamWithContext(parentCtx, opts)
msgs := handle.Messages() // <-chan Message
err := handle.Wait() // blocks until stream ends, returns error from transport or ctx
handle.Close() // cancels and cleans up
```

maria: I like that. Also need to solve auth refresh race — currently token refresh may swap transport mid-stream, causing intermittent 401s. helper should either block Start until token is available or automatically retry on 401 with backoff.

joel: +1 to retry on 401 with idempotent semantics. we can add a small internal state machine: START -> AUTH -> STREAM. Start waits for initial token if refresh in-flight, but still allow user ctx to cancel while waiting.

sara: small DX nit: naming. we have both "StartStream", "Generator.Start", and "Stream" in docs. can we pick a consistent verb pattern (Start/Stream/Open) across SDKs? other languages use Open/streamWithContext.

matt: agreed. propose: OpenStream(ctx, opts) for symmetry with existing Open/Close patterns. keep Generator.Stream as legacy alias for a couple releases.

maria: thanks — I'll open a tiny PR with the helper interface + a sampleapp update showing Cancel via ctx.WithTimeout and auth-retry enabled.

dev-bot: CI check queued for @maria's branch. :robot_face:

joel: thanks — one more ask: add a short example in docs showing an explicit Close() in defer so folks don't leak goroutines. most leaks we've seen come from missing Close calls. :thumbsup:

maria: got it, will add example and a unit test that cancels mid-handshake to catch regressions.
